correctness.rationale: Starting from the exact backward equation with strict positive reset rates, solve the bounded absorbing system and reduce it to the spectral Schur complement. Two positive eigenvalues and superalgebraically small high-mode inverse yield a uniform differentiated expansion. Explicit derivatives prove strict curvature and the unique nonzero Poisson optimum. Substitution and a sign-definite derivative yield the critical-window limit and unique local zero. A separate direct backward-system solver and high-precision spectral evaluation produced 294 finite checks; none is substituted for proof.

value.rationale: When the mean resetting rate is tuned to the globally optimal constant-rate searcher, the leading fluctuating-rate perturbation disappears and its sign cannot be inferred from usual first-order results. The nontrivial positive second-order correction proves that fast environmental disorder is locally harmful there, while the explicit shifted threshold identifies how much above optimum the mean rate must be to make disorder beneficial. This addresses a naturally controllable physical decision boundary rather than an arbitrary perturbative coefficient.
